statement: For the actual joint quotient of the full compact cubic group with finite projective j-line modular level m, every finite coefficient erasure n(1-e_P) fails Selmer lifting at m=3 if3 is not inP, and at m=4 for every finite nonemptyP. On the least rank-one cubic E9, every singleton erasure n(1-e_p), all primesp and all n!=0, already fails at m=3.
depends_on: A.44 abstract lifts; A.61 CM Kummer openness; exact projective modular monodromy and cubic subgroup images; explicit Hesse X3 map; boundary-unit character factorization through the joint kernel; formal primary decomposition; S-squareclass finiteness; Faltings1983 with1984 correction; exact translated-unit identity and local3 valuations
answers: A.12(b) and Lead5: an actual congruence-quotient mechanism for the first named level killing every singleton erasure on the least-conductor curve, with a uniform level4 bound for all finite erasures on cubic twists possessing a rational infinity flex. Supplies precise X3,X4,X5,X7 fibre-product comparison without claiming complete lifting sets.
notes: Gamma_m is explicitly the image of pi1(U) in pi1(E) times over G_Q the finite projective modular quotient. The convention is the j-line with branchorders(3,2,m), not the Legendre lambda-line. Fibre-product genera are4,46,118,343; Hesse maps and matrix images were computed exactly. X3 characters are flex ratios modulo compact unramified characters; the direct geometric-kernel argument proves the arithmetic Kummer characters factor through Gamma3. X4 uses only kappa2(1-J), already the level2 S3-sign quotient; levels are not assumed nested and no minimality claim is made. At erased3 on E9, pro3/quadratic Chebotarev forces the same global unit value at A and A+d1, while g(A+d1)=(zeta+2)/(zeta-y(A)) has an odd local3 ratio valuation for every rational A=nP. q61 supplies an additional exact finite witness. Root and B audited the character/forcing arguments; root approved the uniform local3 proof. No scalar parametrization of originless torsors or arbitrary one-prime alterations is asserted.
